words.definition: An object that children play with.
words.example: The baby loves her new toy.

words.definition: A small model of a person that children play with.
words.example: She plays with her doll all day.

words.definition: A light frame covered with paper or cloth that flies on a string.
words.example: We flew a kite on the beach.

words.definition: A rubber bag filled with air or gas.
words.example: The kids blew up balloons for the party.

words.definition: A small glass ball used in a children's game, or a type of stone.
words.example: He collects marbles.

words.definition: A cup or prize given to a winner.
words.example: The team lifted the trophy.

words.definition: A flat piece of metal given as a prize.
words.example: She won a gold medal.

words.definition: Something given to the winner of a competition.
words.example: First prize is a trip to Spain.

words.definition: A competition.
words.example: He won a cooking contest.

words.definition: A competition to see who is fastest.
words.example: I'm running a race on Sunday.

words.definition: A small piece of stiff paper or plastic.
words.example: I forgot my credit card.

words.definition: A set of numbers or letters used as a secret message or password.
words.example: Enter the four-digit code.

words.definition: A soft hat with a curved front, or a lid.
words.example: He wore a baseball cap.

words.definition: The part of a shirt or coat that goes around your neck, or a band around a pet's neck.
words.example: Her shirt has a white collar.

words.definition: A thick wire that carries electricity or signals.
words.example: I need a longer cable.

words.definition: A series of names, items or numbers written down.
words.example: I made a shopping list.

words.definition: A notice that gives information, or a signal.
words.example: There was a sign on the door.

words.definition: A large bag made of strong material.
words.example: He carried a sack of potatoes.

words.definition: A large piece of cloth for a bed, or a flat piece of paper.
words.example: I need clean sheets for the bed.

words.definition: A long narrow piece of material used to hold or carry something.
words.example: The strap on my bag broke.

words.definition: A friend. Informal.
words.example: Hey, buddy, how's it going?

words.definition: A man. Informal.
words.example: He's a really nice guy.

words.definition: People. Informal.
words.example: Thanks for coming, folks!

words.definition: A friend. Informal.
words.example: He's an old pal of mine.

words.definition: A friend. Common in British English.
words.example: Cheers, mate!

words.definition: A man, or a casual way of addressing a friend.
words.example: Dude, you won't believe what happened.

words.definition: A loving word for someone you care about.
words.example: Thanks, sweetheart.

words.definition: A loving word for someone you love.
words.example: Good night, darling.

words.definition: A polite way to address a man.
words.example: Excuse me, sir. You dropped this.

words.definition: A polite way to address a woman.
words.example: Can I help you, madam?

words.definition: A word that shows a result.
words.example: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

words.definition: A word that adds a contrast, meaning "even though".
words.example: Although it was late, we kept talking.

words.definition: A word that adds a contrast to what was just said.
words.example: I like the apartment. However, it's too far from work.

words.definition: A word that shows a result or conclusion.
words.example: He's sick. Therefore, he won't come to work today.

words.definition: A word that means "if not".
words.example: We'll go to the beach unless it rains.

words.definition: A word that means "at the same time as".
words.example: Don't text while you're driving.

words.definition: A word that gives the starting point or the reason.
words.example: I've been tired since I got home.

words.definition: A word that adds another reason.
words.example: I don't feel like going out. Besides, it's cold.

words.definition: A word that shows what will happen if something does not happen.
words.example: Hurry up. Otherwise, we'll miss the train.

words.definition: Despite that, or a way to change the subject.
words.example: It was raining, but we went anyway.

words.definition: A warm piece of clothing worn outdoors.
words.example: Put on your coat. It's freezing.

words.definition: A jacket and pants made from the same cloth.
words.example: He wore a gray suit.

words.definition: A loose shirt worn by women.
words.example: She wore a silk blouse.

words.definition: A sleeveless piece of clothing worn over a shirt.
words.example: He wore a vest over his shirt.

words.definition: Clothing worn next to your skin under other clothes.
words.example: Pack extra underwear for the trip.

words.definition: Pants. Common in British English.
words.example: He wore black trousers.

words.definition: Comfortable shoes for sports.
words.example: I wear sneakers to work.

words.definition: Soft shoes that you wear indoors.
words.example: She put on her slippers.

words.definition: Gloves that cover your four fingers together.
words.example: The kids wore mittens in the snow.

words.definition: A sweatshirt with a hood.
words.example: He wore a gray hoodie.

words.definition: A person who writes books, articles or stories.
words.example: She's a writer for a magazine.

words.definition: A person who finds and tells news stories.
words.example: The reporter asked the mayor a question.

words.definition: A person who plays or writes music.
words.example: He's a talented musician.

words.definition: A person who works in a library.
words.example: Ask the librarian for help.

words.definition: A person who prepares and sells medicines.
words.example: The pharmacist explained the instructions.

words.definition: A person who works in an office or shop doing simple tasks.
words.example: The clerk gave me a receipt.

words.definition: A person who does tricks that seem like magic.
words.example: The magician pulled a rabbit from his hat.

words.definition: A person who takes photos.
words.example: The photographer took pictures at the wedding.

words.definition: A person who tells jokes to make people laugh.
words.example: The comedian had everyone laughing.

words.definition: A person who writes poems.
words.example: She's a famous poet.

words.definition: To start to be something.
words.example: She became a doctor after ten years of study.

words.definition: To be owned by someone, or to be part of a group.
words.example: Does this umbrella belong to you?

words.definition: To be decided by something else.
words.example: It depends on the weather.

words.definition: To have something as one of the parts.
words.example: The price includes breakfast.

words.definition: To stay in the same place or state.
words.example: Please remain seated until the plane stops.

words.definition: To give the impression of being something.
words.example: You seem tired. Are you okay?

words.definition: To be important.
words.example: It doesn't matter. We can do it tomorrow.

words.definition: To do what you tried to do.
words.example: She worked hard and finally succeeded.

words.definition: To not succeed.
words.example: I failed my driving test the first time.

words.definition: To feel pain or have a problem.
words.example: My grandfather suffers from back pain.

words.definition: A doctor who looks after your teeth.
words.example: I have to see the dentist on Tuesday.

words.definition: A sign that you have an illness.
words.example: A cough is a common symptom of a cold.

words.definition: Harm done to a part of your body.
words.example: He missed the game because of a knee injury.

words.definition: A bad reaction your body has to something like food or pollen.
words.example: I have an allergy to peanuts.

words.definition: An illness like a bad cold, with fever and aching muscles.
words.example: Half the office has the flu.

words.definition: A strip of cloth you wrap around an injury.
words.example: Put a bandage on that cut.

words.definition: A note from a doctor that lets you get a medicine.
words.example: I'm picking up my prescription at the pharmacy.

words.definition: A vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to the hospital.
words.example: Someone call an ambulance!

words.definition: A medical operation in which a doctor cuts into the body.
words.example: She's having surgery on her knee next week.

words.definition: A substance in food that your body needs to stay healthy.
words.example: Do you take a vitamin every day?

words.definition: Shaped like a circle or a ball.
words.example: We sat at a round table.

words.definition: Smooth and level, with no high or low parts.
words.example: The road is flat for the first ten miles.

words.definition: Not wide.
words.example: The street is too narrow for big trucks.

words.definition: Rising or falling sharply.
words.example: The hill is too steep to cycle up.

words.definition: Covered with something that attaches to things.
words.example: My hands are sticky from the juice.

words.definition: Light in color, or having a face that is whiter than normal.
words.example: You look pale. Are you feeling okay?

words.definition: Simple, without decoration or flavor.
words.example: I'll have plain rice, please.

words.definition: Strong, difficult to cut or break, or hard to deal with.
words.example: This steak is a bit tough.

words.definition: Very big.
words.example: They sell giant pizzas at that place.

words.definition: Fairly hard, not soft.
words.example: I like a firm mattress.

words.definition: Programs that run on a computer.
words.example: You need to update the software.

words.definition: A machine made for a particular purpose, like a phone.
words.example: Turn off all electronic devices during takeoff.

words.definition: A group of computers or systems that are connected.
words.example: I can't connect to the network.

words.definition: Facts and information, or the amount of internet you use on a phone.
words.example: I'm almost out of data this month.

words.definition: The set of keys you press to type.
words.example: My keyboard is full of crumbs.

words.definition: A way of connecting to the internet without wires.
words.example: What's the wifi password?

words.definition: Things you wear over your ears to listen to sound privately.
words.example: Put on your headphones. I'm trying to work.

words.definition: A device that puts power into a battery.
words.example: Can I borrow your charger?

words.definition: A flat computer you use by touching the screen.
words.example: She reads books on her tablet.

words.definition: A small computer you can carry and use on your lap.
words.example: He carries his laptop everywhere.
